items.question: Under what condition must concealment be undertaken in the mortal world among the lowest of men?
premises: Concealment is prescribed as a necessary act.
Effort is the means by which concealment is to be applied.
This duty applies specifically in the mortal world among the lowest of men.
items.inference: Concealment must be carried out with effort in the mortal world among the lowest of men.
items.plain_english: What is to be concealed must be concealed with effort in the mortal world among the lowest of men.

items.question: To whom and under what test must a gift be offered according to the stated criterion?
premises: A gift is prescribed as something to be given.
The recipient is one who has been previously accomplished.
That recipient must have been tested for one year.
items.inference: A gift must be given to one previously accomplished who has been tested for one year.
items.plain_english: A gift is to be given to one who was previously accomplished and tested for one year.

items.question: By what positional claim is this chapter identified as originating from Candradvīpa?
premises: The chapter is said to have emerged from Candradvīpa.
It is counted as the fifth in order.
It is designated as a chapter.
items.inference: The fifth chapter is the one that emerged from Candradvīpa.
items.plain_english: The fifth chapter emerged from Candradvīpa.

items.question: By what means does the speaker claim to have come to know the determination of Kaula?
premises: The speaker addresses the lord of Kaulas.
The speaker claims to have become known or to have known through grace.
That knowledge is of the determination of Kaula.
The means cited is the grace of the addressee.
items.inference: By the grace of the lord of Kaulas, the speaker has come to know the determination of Kaula.
items.plain_english: By your grace, O lord of Kaulas, I have come to know the determination of Kaula.

items.question: What two points of inquiry are being raised about the soul and its nature?
premises: A question is raised as to which soul is declared.
A further question is raised as to what the nature of the soul is.
The two inquiries are posed disjunctively.
items.inference: The inquiry concerns both the identity of the declared soul and the nature of the soul.
items.plain_english: Who is that soul that has been declared? Or what is the nature of the soul?

rows.grounds: locative of ka/interrogative fused as given

items.question: In what locus does dissolution occur, and what totality is being requested to be told?
premises: Dissolution is said to go to or occur in some locus.
The particle combination marks emphasis on that locus.
The speaker requests that the whole of that matter be told to them.
items.inference: The speaker asks for the locus of dissolution and for the whole of that matter to be explained.
items.plain_english: And indeed, in what does it go to dissolution? Tell me all of that.

items.question: What set of attributes is being ascribed to that supreme entity in this statement?
premises: That entity is designated as supreme.
It is ascribed partlessness and eternality.
It is ascribed freedom from disease and stainlessness.
items.inference: That entity is the supreme, partless, eternal, disease-free and stainless one.
items.plain_english: He is the supreme, partless, eternal, free from disease and stainless one.

items.question: What identity is established between the soul, the haṃsa, and the power-individual by the relative clause?
premises: The soul is said to be the supreme one.
The relative clause identifies that same one as the haṃsa.
That haṃsa is designated as the power-individual.
items.inference: The soul who is supreme is the haṃsa, designated as the power-individual.
items.plain_english: He is the soul, the supreme one; indeed, he is the haṃsa, the power-individual.

items.question: Where is the wind-filling air said to be situated according to this statement?
premises: The air is designated as wind-filling.
That air is described as situated.
Its locus is said to be in all beings.
items.inference: The wind-filling air is situated in all beings.
items.plain_english: The wind-filling air is situated in all beings.

rows.grounds: present passive of ni-gad third person

items.question: Under what minimal condition is that entity said to be called the supreme Śiva?
premises: That entity is designated by the pronoun.
The condition given is merely the leaving of the body.
Under that condition, it is called the supreme Śiva.
items.inference: Upon merely leaving the body, that entity is called the supreme Śiva.
items.plain_english: He, upon merely leaving the body, is called the supreme Śiva.

rows.grounds: present passive of śru third person

items.question: What kind of teaching is said to be heard in the ear, and by what mode of transmission?
premises: Something abiding in the ear is said to be heard.
The addressee is addressed as goddess.
That thing is described as having come down through tradition in order.
items.inference: O goddess, what abides in the ear and has come down through successive tradition is heard.
items.plain_english: O goddess, that which abides in the ear and has come down through tradition is heard.

items.question: By what means is efficacy attributed in this address to the fair-faced one?
premises: An instrument is indicated by this.
That instrument is specified as mere knowledge.
It is further specified as what has been heard.
The address is made to the fair-faced one.
items.inference: By this mere knowledge, namely what has been heard, effect is attributed in the address to the fair-faced one.
items.plain_english: By this mere knowledge, by what has been heard, O fair-faced one.

items.question: For whom is practice prescribed for six months, and what is specified as the object or condition of that practice?
premises: A person who practices is indicated by the relative pronoun.
The practice is to be undertaken from six months onward.
The object specified is the ochre robe, described as free from bondage.
items.inference: Whoever practices should do so for six months with regard to the ochre robe that is free from bondage.
items.plain_english: Whoever indeed should practice for six months, wearing the ochre robe free from bondage.

items.question: What state and what association are ascribed to one freed from all diseases?
premises: One is described as freed from all diseases.
That one is associated with yogis.
The association is described as union together.
items.inference: One freed from all diseases attains union together with yogis.
items.plain_english: Freed from all diseases, he attains union together with yogis.

items.question: What practice is said to have been told to the addressee, and to whom is it addressed?
premises: This practice of the soul is the object stated.
It has been told to you.
The address is made to Bhairavī.
items.inference: This practice of the soul has been told to you, O Bhairavī.
items.plain_english: This practice of the soul has been told to you, and to you, O Bhairavī.

items.question: To what kind of person is a gift prescribed as to be given?
premises: A gift is prescribed as to be given.
It is to be given to one endowed with all states.
It is to be given to one of resolved mind.
items.inference: A gift is to be given to one endowed with all states and of resolved mind.
items.plain_english: It is to be given to one endowed with all states, to one of resolved mind.

items.question: What restriction is placed on giving the Kaula essence in relation to yoginīs and their origin?
premises: The Kaula essence is not to be given.
A restriction is marked by the adversative particle.
The context relates to yoginīs and what arises from them.
items.inference: The Kaula essence, which has its origin among yoginīs, is not to be given.
items.plain_english: The Kaula essence is not to be given, for it has its origin among yoginīs.

items.question: In what condition is the speaker's body described as being today?
premises: The speaker refers to their own body.
The body is described as pure.
It is described as struck by the veil of ignorance.
items.inference: Today the speaker's pure body is struck by the veil of ignorance.
items.plain_english: Today my pure body is struck by the veil of ignorance.

items.question: What auspicious matter does the speaker now wish to hear concerning time?
premises: The speaker wishes to hear now.
The object of hearing is the deception of time.
That deception is described as auspicious.
items.inference: The speaker now wishes to hear of the auspicious deception of time.
items.plain_english: Now I wish to hear of the auspicious deception of time.

items.question: What assurance is given about the manner in which death is destroyed?
premises: The speaker states that they will tell.
No doubt is said to remain.
It is told how death is destroyed.
items.inference: The speaker tells how death is destroyed, with no doubt remaining.
items.plain_english: I tell it; there is no doubt, that death is destroyed as such.

items.question: Under what condition is even the wise one said to be burning?
premises: Reference is made to the tip of nectar.
Reference is made to the tip of essence.
Even the wise one, while burning, is mentioned with the emphatic particle.
items.inference: Even the wise one, burning at the tip of nectar with the tip of essence, is in that condition.
uncertainties: Exact syntactic relation between the two compound tips remains uncertain from tokens alone.
items.plain_english: Even the wise one, burning, at the tip of nectar with the essence at the tip.

items.question: At what locus and in what manner is the air to be drawn or drunk?
premises: The locus is at the root of the tongue and palate.
Having placed the air there, an action is prescribed.
That action is to drink slowly.
items.inference: Having placed the air at the root of the tongue and palate, one should drink it slowly.
items.plain_english: Having placed the air at the root of the tongue and palate, one should drink it slowly.

rows.grounds: nominative/accusative of yadā+abhyasta fused as given

items.question: Under what temporal condition are old age and death said to be destroyed?
premises: A duration of one year is stated.
That duration is linked to practice when practiced.
Old age and death are said to be destroyed.
items.inference: When practice has been carried out for one year, old age and death are destroyed.
uncertainties: The fused form yadā+abhyastañ is analyzed as given without internal split.
items.plain_english: When practiced for one year, old age and death are destroyed.

rows.grounds: present of kram middle third person

items.question: What immunity is stated for one bitten by great serpents with regard to poison?
premises: Poison is the subject.
It is said not to enter the body.
This holds even for one who has been bitten by great serpents.
items.inference: Poison does not enter the body, even if one has been bitten by great serpents.
items.plain_english: Poison does not enter the body, even if one has been bitten by great serpents.
